prompt_used:
Transform the subject into a sumptuous romantic portrait of a Persian nobleman of the Safavid court, preserving his facial likeness and ethnicity. Dress him in richly woven crimson, madder red and tarnished-gold brocade, layered period garments, a jeweled sash, restrained antique jewelry and an elegant Safavid turban. Likeness is important.
Likeness is essential. maintain expression, micro gestures, imperfections. do not introduce body imperfections.
Do not modify body or head shape to suit period. DO NOT INCREASE WEIGHT
He belongs completely to the period, with a natural, reserved courtly posture and quiet, self-possessed expression. Avoid modern posing and contemporary styling.
Photograph him in an intimate Safavid palace chamber by dim oil-lamp and candlelight, with carved plaster, faded Persian textiles, dark wood and intricate tilework disappearing into shadow.
face should occupy at least 15% of the image. frame from thighs to top of head plus 20% margin above head and sides.
Give the photograph a softly aged, time-worn character: faded crimson, tarnished gold, tobacco brown, warm umber and muted lapis. Slightly desaturated skin and colors, warm lifted blacks, amber haze, subtle grain and softened highlights. Deep velvety shadows with uneven flame falloff.
Romantic and intimate rather than theatrical, like an old Persian court portrait somehow captured through a camera, imperfect, atmospheric and quietly luxurious.
Period objects may be held — a book, a scroll, a cup, prayer beads, a flower. Nothing modern.
